1: O-GlcNAc sites concentrate into regional clusters. A, Original CRTC3 opportunity/site/region tracks with its 340–363 sequence excerpt. B, Close-pair enrichment on matched proteins; 867 of 1,022 pairs are visible on log axes. C, All six radius-dependent fold ratios with archived 95% matched-protein bootstrap intervals; coral identifies radius 10. D, Evidence-restricted and peptide-conditioned analyses use distinct populations and null models. E, Independent-resource comparisons retained from the authored analysis. F, Strongest-effect-first removal with the archived random-removal envelope. Sensitivity analyses are post hoc. See the source manifest for exact inputs.
2: Local composition predicts regional organization. A, Empirical ROC curves for three models on the same 16,253 tiles at or above both median disorder and median S/T fraction; this is a restriction, not exact matching. B, Clustered-versus-isolated acceptor coefficients with archived intervals. C, Cumulative distributions of within-protein AUROC across the same 454 proteins with both tile classes. Means are 0.792 for composition, 0.844 for disorder plus S/T, and 0.874 for the full model, which additionally includes geometry. D, Paired mean AUROC gain from adding composition to the covariates, at five core gaps with minimum three sites and final gap 10. Coral identifies the primary definition (+0.0131; 95% CI 0.0047–0.0211). Protein cohorts differ across definitions; these are post hoc sensitivity checks. E, The existing eight exemplar proteins span the earlier selection range; each assayed span is normalized, with composition scores, S/T fraction, disorder and observed-positive tiles shown. Fixed held-out predictions were reused without refitting.
3: Prediction transfers across species, while local S/T availability persists. A, Archived alignment-free transfer AUROCs and 95% protein-bootstrap intervals; denominators are shown and the dashed line marks the archived 0.80 benchmark. B, Fraction of aligned anchors retaining S/T in the exact ortholog column or in a neighborhood corresponding to ±5 human residues. These measure residue availability, not experimentally demonstrated conservation of O-GlcNAc modification. C, Paired local-minus-exact differences with archived protein-bootstrap intervals and species-specific protein counts. A wider window supplies more opportunities, so the difference alone does not demonstrate selection. Null-calibrated composition and modified-position analyses remain in S3; the earlier model comparisons are preserved in the linked supporting review. No model or interval was refit.
4: Local opportunity accounts for much of the PTM overlap. A, Per-protein observed-minus-expected close-pair fractions at radius 10, replacing the earlier ratio-of-means display. Boxes show median and IQR, whiskers extend to 1.5 IQR, and dots show outliers; all 23,180 protein/PTM records are represented. PTM cohorts differ and lysine modifications have different opportunity universes. B, Archived protein-averaged proline profiles around acceptors. C, Distribution of all 465 paired differences in the number of kinases scoring above the 90th percentile; the archived mean is −5.29 with 95% CI −6.69 to −3.95. D, Four primary ±25-residue local co-occurrence contrasts with archived intervals. E, Length-, S/T- and disorder-conditioned nulls. F, Archived distance-profile difference and interval after covariate matching. These observational controls do not establish biochemical competition.
5: Catalogue case study and internally held-out scanner performance. A, Ten FG nucleoporins, each normalized to its own length; 67 consensus regions are shown on eight proteins. Actual lengths and region counts appear beside the tracks. This is catalogue region membership, not prospective recovery by the scanner. B, Legacy and enhanced average precision in each of five protein-grouped outer folds. C, Complete precision–recall curves from 314,040 fixed held-out tile predictions across 3,535 proteins, with 3,196 positive catalogue tiles. Pooled AP is 0.191 and 0.219; the dashed line is the 1.02% catalogue prevalence. D, Number of catalogue regions recovered versus tiles called across all five training-calibrated settings. Connectors pair calibration settings, not equal calling budgets. Enhanced predictions make more calls at each setting. Tiles overlap and catalogue labels are incomplete; this is grouped internal validation, not prospective validation.
S1: Region-definition and evidence robustness. A, Final grouping-gap sensitivity with the strict core fixed. B, Site-assignment sensitivity. C, Region-length distribution. D, Independent-publication support and largest-study removal. E, Single-protein-removal sensitivity. These retained analyses support Figure 1; the accepted numerical definitions and original source results remain unchanged.
S2: Kinase preferences and co-occurrence sensitivity. A, Ranked cluster-minus-control mean shifts for all 309 kinase matrices; color follows shift sign, not family. B, Individual kinase shifts grouped by family, with family counts, mean ticks and interquartile spans. Vertical jitter separates overlapping points only; single-kinase families have no distribution interval. Kinases share site pairs and are not independent biological replicates. C, All 12 local co-occurrence estimates and archived intervals; 11 include one. No family-level significance test was introduced.
S3: Null calibration and site-landing controls. A/B, Authored similarity metrics, their nulls and excesses. Metrics have different definitions and scales and should not be ranked by excess magnitude. C, Modified-position sensitivity to zero imputation versus excluding zero-variance pairs. D, Projected-window and alignment-free site-landing contrasts answer different questions. E, Selective-axis and additional site-landing controls retained from the earlier main figure. All panels preserve archived data paths and values; this caption must retain the original method-specific details when integrated.
S4: Sensitivity to calling thresholds. A, Retained core sites. B, Site-set Jaccard similarity to the primary definition. C, Composition-only within-protein discrimination. D, Increment from adding composition to disorder and S/T, with archived protein-bootstrap intervals. Shape and color encode minimum site count and the coral ring marks the primary definition. All 15 archived core-gap/site-count model settings are retained; the sensitivity analysis is post hoc.
